end.summary:
Practised showing that consecutive odd numbers starting at 1 sum to square numbers.
Saanvi calculated 1+3=4, 1+3+5=9, and 1+3+5+7=16.
They connected 25 with a 5-by-5 square on a geoboard.
The L-shaped growth pattern and the required starting sequence remained unclear.
They corrected the mix-up that odd + odd gives an even number.
end.parentNote: Asha practised the pattern by adding consecutive odd numbers from 1 and linking the totals to square numbers. Saanvi used repeated addition correctly for several examples and connected 25 with a 5-by-5 square. They initially treated any odd-number run as producing a square; this was not corrected by the end of the lesson, although the odd-plus-odd parity mix-up was corrected later. At home, draw 1-by-1, 2-by-2, 3-by-3, and 4-by-4 squares and count only the new outer L-shaped dots each time.
